identity.description: Cost-effective single-cell Li-Ion/Li-polymer battery protection IC with factory-programmed overcharge, over-discharge, charge/discharge overcurrent and short-circuit protection driving two external low-side NMOS FETs, 8 V operating BAT input and BAT - 25 V V- tolerance
identity.variant_differences: OVP 4.280 V / 1 s, UVP 2.800 V / 96 ms, OCC -0.090 V / 6 ms, OCD 0.090 V / 16 ms, SCD 0.3 V / 250 µs

pinout.name: COUT
pinout.function: Gate drive output for the external charge FET, driven from internal circuitry connected to the BAT supply; goes from high to low when a fault is detected to turn the charge FET off. Referenced to V-.

pinout.name: DOUT
pinout.function: Gate drive output for the external discharge FET, driven from internal circuitry connected to the BAT supply; goes from high to low when a fault is detected to turn the discharge FET off. Referenced to VSS.

pinout.name: VSS
pinout.function: Ground pin; cell negative reference for the internal cell voltage measurement and the differential overcurrent sensing against V-.

pinout.name: BAT
pinout.function: VDD pin: device supply input connected to the positive terminal of the battery pack.

pinout.name: V-
pinout.function: Input pin for charger negative voltage; sense node that, together with VSS, forms the differential measurement for charge/discharge overcurrent and load short-circuit detection. Internally pulled up to BAT through R(V-D) (100–550 kΩ) in the over-discharge state and sunk to VSS by the constant current I(V-S) in the discharge overcurrent state.

supplies.name: BAT
supplies.notes: Device supply from the cell positive terminal. Device operating range BAT – VSS = 1.5 V to 8 V, BAT – V- = 1.5 V to 28 V. Recommended maximum operation is 8 V on the BAT input pin. Current consumption in NORMAL mode 4 µA typ / 5.5 µA max at BAT = 3.8 V, V- = 0 V; power-down mode consumption 0.1 µA max at BAT = V- = 1.5 V. Typical values in the DC table are stated at TA = 25 °C and BAT = 3.6 V; min/max over TA = -40 °C to 85 °C and BAT = 3 V to 4.2 V. Over-discharge (power-down) state is released when a charger is connected and the delta between V- and BAT exceeds 1.3 V.

supplies.name: V-
supplies.notes: Charger-negative sense input (Pack-). Recommended range BAT - 25 V to BAT; absolute maximum BAT - 28 V to BAT + 0.3 V. Internally pulled up to BAT through R(V-D) = 100–550 kΩ in the over-discharge state; sunk to VSS by I(V-S) = 8–24 µA in the discharge overcurrent state. Neither R(V-D) nor I(V-S) is connected in the charge overcurrent state, and I(V-S) is inactive in power-down/over-discharge.

external_components.key_specs: Low-side NMOS, logic level: Vdss, RDS(on) and Vgs to be designed according with the circuit requirements, Imax defined to survive the short-circuit condition for max delay timer. The combined CHG + DSG on-resistance must be designed according with the OCD threshold to trips just above maximum discharge current. RDS(on) needs to satify the OCC threshold for the maximum charge current during operation. Total RDS(on) must include worst-case temperature derating and the available gate drive Vgs.

designer_notes: BQ29707 configuration as printed in the Device Comparison Table: OVP 4.280 V with 1 s delay, UVP 2.800 V with 96 ms delay, OCC -0.090 V with 6 ms delay, OCD 0.090 V with 16 ms delay, SCD 0.3 V with 250 µs delay. All thresholds and delays are factory programmed and cannot be changed in the application.

Recovery delays are fixed: OVP recovery delay = 12 ms, UVP/OCC/OCD recovery delay = 8 ms. The recovery timer starts as soon as the fault is triggered, and the device only begins checking for a recovery condition once that timer expires — it is not a delay between recovery condition and FET turn-on.

The device drives two low-side NMOS FETs in the pack negative path. COUT is referenced to V- and DOUT to VSS; 'H' on either output must exceed the external logic-level FET threshold to be regarded as ON.
When the battery is connected for the first time the discharging circuit may not be enabled; in that case short V- to VSS, or connect a charger between the Pack+ and Pack- terminals.

Sizing rule from the design example: total on-resistance across the two series FETs = OCD threshold / maximum discharge current (100 mV / 7 A = 14.3 mΩ). That same resistance at the 4.5 A maximum charge current gives 65 mV, so a 70 mV OCC option is acceptable. Include worst-case RDS(on) derating over temperature and the available Vgs in the budget.

The FETs must survive the short-circuit current for the maximum 350 µs delay; the only limiting element is pack voltage divided by (cell resistance + 2 × FET RDS(on) + trace resistance), which drove the Imax > 50 A requirement in the example.

An RC filter on BAT (330 Ω series, 0.1 µF to ground) is required for noise immunity and to keep the device operating through sharp negative transients; the resistor also limits current if the system is connected in reverse.

TI recommends a high-impedance 5 MΩ resistor across the gate-source of each external FET to bleed the gate-source capacitance; the typical application schematic marks this external gate-source resistor as optional.

In the over-discharge (power-down) state V- is internally pulled to BAT through R(V-D); the V- to BAT difference is then 1.3 V or lower and supply current drops to the power-down level. The power-down state releases when a charger brings the V- to BAT delta above 1.3 V.

Over-discharge release depends on the charger voltage seen at V-: below -0.7 V the device releases as soon as the cell exceeds V(UVP); above -0.7 V it releases only when the cell exceeds V(UVP) + hysteresis.

In the discharge overcurrent state, V- and VSS are joined by the constant current sink I(V-S) and R(V-D) is disconnected; with a load attached V- sits at BAT potential and with the load removed it goes to VSS (BAT/2). Recovery occurs when the load impedance rises enough for V- to return to BAT - 1 V or lower, or when a charger is connected.

In the charge overcurrent state neither R(V-D) nor I(V-S) is connected; recovery requires removing the charger so V- returns to the charge overcurrent detection voltage or higher. Charge overcurrent detection does not work in the over-discharge state.

If the cell is overcharged above V(OVP) and the voltage does not fall back below V(OVP) under a heavy load, discharge overcurrent and load short-circuit detection do not function until the cell voltage drops below V(OVP).

If a charger is connected after an overcharge detection, the overcharge status does not release even when the cell falls below the release threshold; it releases when the V- voltage exceeds the OCD threshold after the charger is removed.

Zero-voltage charging is allowed when the charger applies at least V(0CHG) = 1.7 V; the 0 V charge feature has higher priority than charge overcurrent detection, so charging is forced and OCC is disabled while the cell is below the over-discharge threshold. Below V(0INH) = 0.75 V the charge FET gate is held at Pack- to inhibit charging; the inhibit function is present in all BQ297xx configurations. Some cell vendors do not recommend charging a depleted cell — consult the battery supplier.

The detection delay timers run from an internal 10 kHz oscillator. A discharge overcurrent below the short-circuit threshold trips after t(OCDD); above the short-circuit threshold DOUT is pulled low after the much shorter t(SCCD).

Layout: give the external power FETs sufficient thermal spreading for worst-case power delivery, keep the connection between the two power FETs very short so no extra drop appears in the fault sense path, and place the BAT RC filter close to the IC terminal.
The design example this data comes from assumes a 4.5 V to 7 V input voltage range, 7 A maximum discharge current and 4.5 A maximum charge current.
